name: Can
hook: Four musicians, two of them Stockhausen's students, who jammed for hours and then edited the tape into records.
blurb: Can started in Cologne in 1968. Holger Czukay on bass and Irmin Schmidt on keyboards had both studied with the composer Karlheinz Stockhausen. With Jaki Liebezeit on drums and Michael Karoli on guitar, they recorded long improvised sessions and then edited them on tape, the way Stockhausen's studio worked, until they had a record. Czukay was as much an editor as a bassist, and the band treated recording as composing, not as capturing a performance. Liebezeit played one pattern for many minutes without changing it. The end year is 1979, when the band stopped working together regularly, though there were reunions afterwards. Punk and post-punk musicians in Britain loved the band, which is well attested by the musicians' own record choices, John Lydon's above all.

signatureTracks.title: Halleluhwah
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Eighteen minutes on one drum pattern, from Tago Mago. The groove other bands copied.

signatureTracks.title: Aumgn
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Also Tago Mago. No beat for long stretches, voices stretched into drones: the Cologne studio inside a rock band.
